vowels.note: e, ai, o, au are always pronounced long (guru) in Sanskrit, even though they look like single letters.

mahaprana.description: Aspirated consonants — pronounced with an audible puff of breath, distinct from their unaspirated pair.

retroflexConsonants.description: Pronounced with the tongue curled back to the roof of the mouth, distinct from the dental version of the same letter.

stressRules.description: A syllable (guru / heavy) is stressed longer when it has a long vowel, is followed by a conjunct consonant, or ends in an anusvara (ṃ) or visarga (ḥ). Otherwise it is light (laghu) and pronounced quickly. The last syllable of each quarter-verse (pada) is treated as heavy by convention.

commonMistakes: Flattening aspirated consonants (bh, dh, kh, gh, ph) into their unaspirated pair.
Not distinguishing retroflex ṇ/ṭ/ḍ from their dental counterparts.
Rushing through conjunct consonants instead of giving them their full heavy length.
Dropping the visarga (ḥ) at the end of words instead of a soft breathy release.
